name.text: Testing on Line of best fit by dragging, order and classification

questiontext.text:
The number of hours spent practising per week \((x)\) and the number of mistakes made in a recital \((y)\) were recorded for 5 students. The mean practice hours is \(\bar{x}={@xm@}\) and the mean number of mistakes is \(\bar{y}={@ym@}\). Two of the plotted points are \(A({@ax@},{@ay@})\) and \(B({@bx@},{@by@})\).

1) Drag the red marker onto that point where the line of best fit must pass through.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="rM" width="520px" height="480px"]] var AX={#ax#}, AY={#ay#}, BX={#bx#}, BY={#by#}; var XMAX={#float(xmaxw)#}, YMAX={#float(ymaxw)#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-1, YMAX, XMAX, -1.5], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); brd.create('text',[XMAX-0.2, -0.8, 'Practice hours (x)'],{anchorX:'right',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('text',[0.2, YMAX-0.4, 'Mistakes (y)'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('point',[AX,AY],{name:'A',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3,label:{offset:[8,6]}}); brd.create('point',[BX,BY],{name:'B',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3,label:{offset:[8,6]}}); var M = brd.create('point',[1,1],{name:'M',color:'#cc0000',fillColor:'#cc0000',size:5,snapToGrid:true,snapSizeX:1,snapSizeY:1,label:{offset:[8,-2],cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}}); brd.create('text',[-0.8, YMAX-2, function(){ return 'M = ('+Math.round(M.X())+', '+Math.round(M.Y())+')'; }],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:13,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}); stack_jxg.bind_point(rM, M); [[/jsxgraph]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prtMean]]

2) How do you draw a line of best fit? Put the steps below into the correct order.

[[parsons input="ansSteps"]] {# parsons_encode(proof_steps) #} [[/parsons]]
[[input:ansSteps]] [[validation:ansSteps]] [[feedback:prtSteps]]

3) State the gradient and the type of relationship.

Gradient: [[input:ansGrad]] [[validation:ansGrad]] [[feedback:prtGrad]]
Relationship: [[input:ansRel]] [[validation:ansRel]] [[feedback:prtRel]]

generalfeedback.text:
1) By the mean-point method the line must pass through \(\left(\bar{x},\bar{y}\right)=({@xm@},{@ym@})\).

2) To draw the line of best fit:

  1. Plot the mean point \(({@xm@},{@ym@})\) and mark it clearly (e.g. a crossed circle labelled M).
  2. Lay a transparent ruler across the grid.
  3. Pivot the ruler through the mean point so the remaining points are balanced evenly above and below the line.
  4. Draw a single, clean, straight line right across the grid.

3) As \(x\) increases, \(y\) [[ if test="is(sgn=1)" ]] increases, so the gradient is positive and there is a positive relationship. [[ else ]] decreases, so the gradient is negative and there is a negative relationship (more practice, fewer mistakes). [[/ if ]]

[[jsxgraph width="480px" height="440px"]] var AX={#ax#}, AY={#ay#}, BX={#bx#}, BY={#by#}, XM={#xm#}, YM={#ym#}, SL={#float(slope)#}; var XMAX={#float(xmaxw)#}, YMAX={#float(ymaxw)#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-1, YMAX, XMAX, -1.5], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); brd.create('text',[XMAX-0.2, -0.8, 'Practice hours (x)'],{anchorX:'right',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('text',[0.2, YMAX-0.4, 'Mistakes (y)'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('functiongraph',[function(x){ return YM + SL*(x-XM); }, 0, XMAX-0.3],{strokeColor:'#1f4fd8', strokeWidth:2, highlight:false}); brd.create('point',[AX,AY],{name:'A',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3,label:{offset:[8,6]}}); brd.create('point',[BX,BY],{name:'B',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3,label:{offset:[8,6]}}); brd.create('point',[XM,YM],{name:'M',fixed:true,color:'#cc0000',fillColor:'#cc0000',size:4,label:{offset:[8,-2],cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}}); [[/jsxgraph]]

falsefeedback.text: Compare \(A\) and \(B\): as \(x\) increases, does \(y\) rise or fall? That gives the sign of the gradient.
The line of best fit passes through the mean point \((\bar{x},\bar{y})=({@xm@},{@ym@})\). Drag the marker there.
A negative gradient means a negative relationship, and a positive gradient a positive one.
Plot the mean point first, then place and pivot the ruler through it, and finally draw the line.
